senses: To descend a steep or vertical drop using a rope with a mechanical friction device or (classic abseil) by wrapping the rope around the body.
ety: From German abseilen, from ab- (“down”) + Seil (“rope”).

senses: The practice of adhering (often excessively) to methods.
examples: Descartes's methodism with its regulative criterion leads him to explicitly deny that accidentally true belief qualifies as knowledge.

senses: A fiscal period of fifteen years, instituted by Constantine in 313 C.E. (but counting from 1st September 312), used throughout the Middle Ages as a way of dating events, documents etc.
A declaration or official announcement.
The decree made by Roman emperors which fixed the property tax for the next fifteen years.
ety: From Old French indiction or its source, Latin indictiōnem, accusative singular of indictiō, from indicere.

senses: The sport of skiercross.
examples: Then in 2000, he won the skicross gold at the X Games against professional skiers.

senses: A person who remodels or does remodeling.
Synonym of juvenile hall (a youth detention centre).
A minor (youth); especially, synonym of juvenile delinquent.
ety: From juvenile + -ie with elision; morphologically analogous to bougie = bourgeoisie + -ie/-y.

senses: Resembling or characterised by lines.
The act of solubilizing something, of rendering it soluble.
A stepbrother.
The extent to which something is collinear.
An outer space laboratory.
examples: Two aspects of altered immunity must be dealt with before man can exist for extended periods in space capsules, skylabs, or sealabs.
What are the scientists up to, apart from perfecting impenetrable food packaging and orbiting skylabs?
With the growing possibility of a global nuclear accident, untold genetic defects, falling skylabs, and the unleasing of powers science cannot control people are once more “off center.”

senses: A soup cooked with meat and starchy plants (such as roots or plantains), usually eaten for lunch.
examples: Sancocho is the name of a hearty Caribbean stew. This meatless version features potatoes, carrots, and West Indian pumpkin, a huge gourd with a vibrant orange flesh and sweet flavor.
Is it bouillabaisse, bourride, burrida, cacciucco, solianka, matelote, sancochos, opera de pescado, or zuppa di pesce?
And Orlando is sipping beer and eating sancocho at his favorite café.

senses: The milky latex of the sapodilla tree, used after coagulation as the principal ingredient of chewing gum.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish chicle, from a Nahuan language; compare Classical Nahuatl tzictli.

senses: Anything petty or insignificant.
ety: From Middle English sprotte, from Old English sprot. Older source is unknown. Cognate with German Sprotte, Dutch sprot. Compare sprout.

senses: Sea trout, a subspecies of brown trout (Salmo trutta morpha trutta).
Being or making a whooping sound; characterized by whoops.
Appropriate to or characteristic of a slattern.
examples: Being a light-complexioned woman, she wore light clothes, as most blondes will, and appeared, in preference, in draggled sea-green, or slatternly sky-blue.

senses: Playful, coltish.
Interested in sport.
Sporty, good at sport.
A land at the periphery of a heartland.
A Japanese dessert consisting of a large mochi stuffed with red bean paste.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 大福 (daifuku, “very filling”).
examples: It’s easy to grab plastic-wrapped daifuku at Japanese grocery stores in New York, and to spot boxes of mochi ice cream in supermarket freezer aisles.

senses: A vegetable pea (Pisum sativum) eaten when immature.
ety: Borrowed from French mangetout, from mange (“eat”) + tout (“all”), since even the pod is edible.

senses: The wood of such trees and shrubs.
ety: From dag + wood, from dag (“a sharp object”).

senses: A person or device that calibrates.
A type of thought-form regarded as capable of independent action, with a persistent personality and identity; a kind of modern imaginary friend.
ety: Borrowed from Tibetan སྤྲུལ་པ (sprul pa, “emanation, magical creation”), equivalent to a calque of Sanskrit निर्मित (nirmita, “build”) or निर्माण (nirmāṇa, “build”).

senses: A person who transcribes.
A writer of transcripts.
A small box.
A nautical compass.
The box in which ashes are stored for Ash Wednesday.
ety: From Latin pyxis (“small box”). Doublet of box, piseog, and pyx.

senses: One who or that which treats.
A vessel used to treat oil-water emulsions by any of several mechanisms so that the oil can be accepted by the pipeline or transport.
A traditional open-sided dwelling built by the Native Americans of Florida.
Any small anadromous fish of the family Osmeridae, found in the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and in lakes in North America and northern part of Europe.
ety: From Middle English smelt, from Old English smelt, from Proto-West Germanic *smelt, from Proto-Germanic *smeltaz.

senses: A musical note equal to two (or occasionally three) breves or whole notes.
Capable of being moved by air.
A potentate; often used as a term of respect.

A lupin bean, a yellow legume seed of a Lupinus plant (usually Lupinus luteus), used as feed for sheep and cattle and commonly eaten in the Mediterranean area and in Latin America although toxic if prepared improperly.
ety: From Middle English lupyne, lupine, from Old French lupin, from Latin lupīnus (“pertaining to the wolf”), because of the wolf-like “fang” within the blossom. It has also been linked to an assumed depletion of nutrients in the soil.

senses: A person who studies methodology, or applies its principles.
examples: Reliability, as a main index of measurement quality, has attracted an enormous amount of interest among methodologists and substantive researchers over the past century (e.g., McDonald, 1999).

senses: A political unit that is populated by and run in the interest of an ethnic group.
examples: Throuples with only white people are so funny they're like hi this is my starter ethnostate we're all in love

senses: intimidated or subjugated
spiritual power or psychic ability
To be close or nearby each other.
A sandwich, usually with a hot or cold savoury filling buttered in a barmcake. The most common are chips, bacon, sausage and egg.
ety: Clipping of buttered sandwich or bun + -y. Compare Saterland Frisian Buutje (“buttered bread (sandwich)”).

senses: A finely ground relatively pure form of silicas used as a paint filler etc.
